problem_type: A conditional fact baked into an unconditional message
symptom: The first time a user connects a provider and validation fails, the message says the previous key and connection are unchanged, although no previous key exists.
direct_cause: The clause lives inside credential.invalid and credential.validationUnavailable, and the layer that throws them never consults apiKeysByVendor, so it cannot know whether anything was preserved.
class_root: A statement whose truth depends on state was stored as part of a fixed string, which places it beyond the reach of the only layer that can evaluate it.
affected_population: Every credential validation failure on every adapted platform, first connection and key replacement alike
entry_points: Save-and-verify on the adapted-platform connect page (upsertVendorApiKey)
Pre-first-use revalidation of a pending credential
invariants: The preserved-key clause appears only when a previous credential actually exists
The decision is made in the layer that can read the catalog, never guessed from a substring downstream
The connect page states whether a key is stored on this machine, derived from state rather than written as a separate failure-copy branch

door_reduction.why_not: Five throw sites but one decision: all of them now call the same credentialFailure(), which is the only place that reads apiKeysByVendor and decides whether to append the clause. Collapsing the throws would merge genuinely different verdicts (no key, no base URL, liveness-probe auth rejection, model-list auth rejection, vendor missing) that the caller distinguishes. The three added doors are the message table, the comment-only seed correction and the renderer's derived stored-key line; none of them decides the clause.

generality_proof: Every path that can produce these two messages goes through validateCandidateCredential or revalidatePendingCredential, and both now compose the clause through the one helper; a repository-wide grep finds no other construction of either message.

shared_boundaries.responsibility: Own the single reading of 'did a previous credential exist' and compose the failure sentence from it

same_class_entry_points.evidence: Its own missing-vendor throw no longer carries the clause either; there is nothing to preserve when the vendor does not exist
Renders the raw main-process sentence unchanged and adds a stored-key line derived from saved state, not a second copy branch

recurrence.reason: Any reassurance clause written into a fixed error string (nothing was lost, your draft is safe, the previous value is kept) becomes a lie in the situation where it does not hold.
same_class_scan: Read every credential.* entry in electron/i18n.ts and separated the state-dependent clauses from the unconditional description

prevention.invariant: The conditional clause is a separate message composed by the one function that can evaluate the condition.
prevention.failure_mode: A new throw site that skips the helper produces the bare description, which is still true; it can never produce a false reassurance.
prevention.strategy: Split the conditional sentence out of the fixed string and move the decision to the layer holding the state, instead of deleting the clause downstream by substring.

legacy_paths.rationale: The clause no longer exists inside the two descriptions; there is no string from which a downstream reader could still emit it unconditionally.

migration: No persisted data changes. Message text only.
residual_risks: builtinVendorSeeds.ts is touched in this batch only to correct a comment that had become false (the liveness probe is now paid at connect time, outside the spend gate). The behaviour it describes is unchanged and is recorded as TODO T-MO-10 pending a product decision.

invariant_owner_layer.rationale: That module is the only layer holding both the verdict and the catalog, so it is the only layer that can decide whether anything was preserved.

internal_only_reason: Whether a previous credential exists for a vendor is a fact about this repository's own catalog store; no external document can decide it.

dependency_lifecycle.rationale: No third-party dependency is involved; the fix is entirely inside this repository's own modules.
